The issue stems from the `PosixParser` in the Apache Commons CLI library. The `parse` method in `PosixParser` is supposed to parse the command line options according to the specified options, arguments, and properties. However, there seems to be a problem with how the default options are processed.

Based on the current bug report, it appears that when the `Properties` instance passed to the `parse` method contains an option that doesn't accept arguments and has a default value that isn't evaluated to "true," the processing of the properties is stopped prematurely, leading to the remaining options not being handled.

Looking at the `parse` method in `PosixParser`, it delegates the actual parsing to another `parse` method in `Parser` class with an additional boolean parameter `stopAtNonOption`. This boolean parameter seems relevant to the issue described in the bug report, where processing stops prematurely.

To resolve the issue, the `stopAtNonOption` parameter in the `parse` method call within `PosixParser` may need to be adjusted to ensure that all options are processed correctly, regardless of the default values in the `Properties` instance.

Next, let's suggest the methods that would be the best locations to be fixed.
```java
org.apache.commons.cli.Parser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], java.util.Properties)
org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLineParser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
